claude.sample_unit: survey respondents in the held-out test set (NSDUH 2015-2019)

links.outcome: Whether clinically weighted metrics, CIs, and threshold choice change model ranking versus raw accuracy
links.effect: Raw accuracy ranked CSBT-Untuned highest (0.867) but it detected only 38.5% of misuse cases; balanced accuracy/CDPS ranked CSBT-Tuned highest (0.696). Bootstrap CIs showed CSBT-Tuned and RUSBoost overlap.
links.quote: WEAS reversed this ordering, ranking CSBT-Tuned highest (0.696), followed by RUSBoost (0.690) and CSBT-Untuned (0.658).

links.outcome: Effect of decision threshold choice on sensitivity, false positives, and net benefit
links.effect: Lowering threshold to 0.33 raised sensitivity from 38.5% to 51.3% and false positives from 119 to 207, reducing PPV from 42.2% to 35.9%; model preference shifted with cost ratio (crossover c_FN≈3.03).
links.quote: The threshold reduction that increased CSBT-Tuned sensitivity from 38.5% to 51.3% simultaneously increased false positives from 119 to 207, reducing PPV from 42.2% to 35.9%.

links.outcome: Leakage-free preprocessing and strict holdout test evaluation
links.effect: Preprocessing fit on training only, target-leakage variables excluded, and test set used once; validation performance consistent with test. However, only internal random split of one survey dataset, no external validation.
links.quote: Across all three models, validation set performance was consistent with test set results.

unlisted_practices: Clinically weighted composite metrics (CDPS, CPUS, WEAS, CEPM) with swing-weight expert elicitation
Cost-ratio crossover analysis for model selection
Decision curve analysis and cost-effectiveness analysis of classifiers
Learning curve convergence as a model disqualification criterion

links.outcome: clinical metrics revealed hidden poor sensitivity
links.effect: CSBT-Untuned had 86.7% raw accuracy but missed 61.5% positives; WEAS ranked CSBT-Tuned highest, 0.696 vs 0.658.
links.quote: The results demonstrate that while CSBT-Untuned achieved the highest raw accuracy of 86.7%, it missed 61.5% of positive cases.

links.outcome: threshold tuning sensitivity and false positives
links.effect: Threshold 0.33 increased sensitivity from 38.5% to 51.3%, but false positives rose from 119 to 207 and PPV fell from 42.2% to 35.9%.
links.quote: The threshold reduction that increased CSBT-Tuned sensitivity from 38.5% to 51.3% simultaneously increased false positives from 119 to 207, reducing PPV from 42.2% to 35.9%.

links.effect: Over thresholds 0.10 to 0.30, INB was 0.00650 for RUSBoost, 0.00621 for CSBT-Tuned, and 0.00570 for CSBT-Untuned.
links.quote: RUSBoost achieved the highest integrated net benefit over the full screening range (0.10 to 0.30), with an INB of 0.00650 compared to 0.00621 for CSBT-Tuned and 0.00570 for CSBT-Untuned.

unlisted_practices: Structured swing-weight elicitation to set clinical composite-metric weights
Penalty-matrix crossover analysis for asymmetric error costs
Decision-curve and cost-effectiveness modeling for classifier selection
Learning-curve convergence checks as a deployment-readiness screen

links.outcome: high raw accuracy concealing poor positive class detection
links.effect: CSBT-Untuned achieved 86.7% raw accuracy but missed 61.5% of positive cases (sensitivity 38.5%, 139 false negatives)
links.quote: The results demonstrate that while CSBT-Untuned achieved the highest raw accuracy of 86.7%, it missed 61.5% of positive cases.
